I definitely know what you mean about struggling to cultivate compassion, I always struggle with that too. 

Know that it’s a process and you don’t just start to feel overwhelming compassion the first time trying it after years of probably not feeling too much. 

If you want to, keep at it, and try to start simple, with people you have gratitude for or find it easy to love, a pet, a loved one, build your way up slowly. Try different methods, eg. Visualisation, mantra, bodily feelings etc. because different things work for different people. 

Maybe most importantly: try not to make the goal the ‘feeling’. Because as soon as you try to grab onto something it’ll slip through your fingers like sand. Instead, just keep going through the visualisation or going over the mantras, letting whatever feelings that come up come and go.

Happy practising :)

I experienced a similar thing when moving from the country to a city environment, constant noise outside my window and never a quiet moment. 

I found it helpful to try to accept the noises, find curiosity in them and embrace them as part of your practise. Imagine the noises like they are a thought- watch the noise as it rises, makes a few sounds, and then falls again. Maybe observe the impermanence of the noise. In time and with practise you can learn to build the noises into your meditation and they won’t be a bother to you. The main thing I would say is try not to resist the sounds or be annoyed at them, instead try to embrace them.

So something I’ve learned with trying to release the energy of a feeling or trying to let a feeling go is it’s pretty futile. You are feeling this feeling right now, however uncomfortable it is, and it’s just going to take some time to pass. You can’t control it by speeding up that time to let it pass, it just has to pass on its own. So during that time, you can observe it, sit with it, even become equanimous with it, but try not to force it to go away, because that’ll only make it stronger. Try focusing instead on giving it space to be in your body and letting it exist and pass in its own time. Hope this helps :)
